title: Latest native capability declarations govern future negotiation and preserve confirmed media
scope: Isolated local macOS arm64 actual signed native QUIC peers/public Rust SDK for EdDSA and ES256, decoded PCMA duplex, controlled Core declaration guards and native negotiation metadata tests. No Linux, remote, browser or external provider qualification.
implementation: Only the original current physical native peer may declare capabilities. The Service holds its actual Store source fence and exact credential, participant/member epoch, Device, Endpoint, runtime generation, stream revision and owner. Pure callbacks match the exact authorized envelope and descriptor without Core or Store reentry.

Core serializes a synchronous leaf metadata commit with controller stream and credential changes using state/credential try-locks. Wrong credential/revision, held mutation state, held credential and shutdown refuse before the callback. No ports, bindings, revision or media clocks change.

The actual native broker retains confirmed capabilities and the latest complete declaration separately under one mutex. It installs declarations under the real parameter request slot. Completed historical replay never reapplies an older declaration. Prepared subscription/codec plans carry the declaration generation and are checked after acquiring the real request slot, before starting an exchange.

The shared native descriptor parser keeps initial-offer validation strict. Declaration mode permits empty/zero withdrawal and bounded future extension metadata. Unknown unsupported protocol/codec values cannot grant engine support or assurance. Existing local, Endpoint and Session ceilings still apply.

New explicit codec choices and new logical/directional/format bindings use only the latest declaration. Exact already confirmed bindings can remain in an effective validation snapshot for source selector changes or untouched media. A withdrawn format cannot be borrowed from an unrelated retained binding for a new selection.

Connect resolves the actual prepared remote capabilities for a current control operation and remembers only successfully confirmed selected formats for existing packet IO. Declarations alone do not change media authority. Packet paths still require actual active bindings and current Store/Endpoint/Session permission.

Incoming descriptor replacement and durable operation completion retain the prior schema82 transaction and original replay/recovery rules. This phase adds no storage schema, compatibility or downgrade path. Server HTTP/OpenAPI documents future-negotiation semantics and the native-only physical-peer boundary.
actual_cases: Both signature algorithms: start with a PCMU-only target in a Session that allows PCMU and PCMA. A PCMA update is refused before declaration. Declare PCMU, replace it with PCMA, replay the older PCMU operation and preserve PCMA as the latest declaration. Original PCMU audio remains usable.

Perform a separate actual codec update with a signed parameter offer and answer, observe the new handle/revision, and decode PCMA audio in both directions. Withdraw the descriptor, replay the old PCMA advertisement and observe withdrawal preserved; a future PCMA codec choice is refused.
After withdrawal, update an existing source selector without another parameter exchange and decode audio in both directions through the retained PCMA binding.

Existing actual receipt, named-scope, false-assurance, foreign physical/participant, stale revision, HTTP refusal and journal fault/recovery cases still pass. The selected regression also covers real lifecycle/quality, stream/data controls, consultation privacy, provider partial-write custody and startup ownership.

upstream_patch.source: G6-046 native capability declarations update future negotiation under the exact current physical/source authority without touching active media. Separate negotiated and declared catalogs, protect prepared plans with declaration generations under the real request slot, preserve actual retained bindings while refusing new withdrawn formats, and serialize the local metadata commit with controller credential/stream state. Actual gained-codec and withdrawal behavior remain to be qualified through Connect.
